renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: strand_signal_genome_view
  title: Strand signal along the genome
  description: |-
    Each bar is a 250 kb window of the genome, drawn from its start to its end, with the height of the combined plus and minus strand signal of one library and one lane per library. It answers where along the genome a library holds its reads.
    How to read: lanes that follow one another peak at the same windows when libraries capture the same transcription. A window that towers over its neighbours in one lane only is a hotspot of that library, for instance a repeat array, so compare the lanes before reading it as biology.
    Note: the signal is scaled to parts per million of each library, so lanes compare in shape and not in depth. bedtools genomecov defines no cut-off for coverage.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the 95th percentile of the window signal of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bedtools. Windows above it are the hottest of the rows on show.
    Source: https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/genomecov.html
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    facet_by_sample: true
    score_title: Signal (log2 of parts per million + 1)
    score_threshold_stat: p95
  roles:
    chr: chromosome
    pos: start
    end: end
    score: log2_signal
    sample: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: strand_signal_track
  title: Strand signal per chromosome
  description: |-
    Each point on a line is a 250 kb window, placed at its centre, with the combined plus and minus strand signal of one library in parts per million. It answers how the signal varies along one chromosome and between libraries.
    How to read: parallel lines mean libraries read the chromosome the same way. A line that departs from the others over a region marks a library with a local gain or loss of signal, worth a look in the genome view or the browser.
    Note: bedtools genomecov defines no cut-off for coverage, so no line or band is drawn.
    Source: https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/genomecov.html
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: chromosome
    position: position
    end: end
    value: signal_rpm
    sample: sample

- component: card
  title: Typical window signal
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median signal of a 250 kb window, as log2 of parts per million plus one, and the box shows the spread over windows. It answers how much signal a typical window of the genome holds.
    How to read: a wide box with a long upper whisker means a few windows hold much more than the rest, which is the pattern of a hotspot or a poorly depleted library. The log scale is used because window signal spans orders of magnitude.
  column: log2_signal
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Plus-strand share of a window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of a window's signal that falls on the plus strand, shown against 100 percent. It answers whether the two strands are read evenly along the genome.
    How to read: a value far from 50 means one strand dominates, which can be a protocol or strandedness problem, or simply the genes of a region that all lie on one strand. Check the per-library tile on the summary before drawing a conclusion.
    Note: bedtools genomecov reports one strand at a time with the -strand option, and publishes no balance cut-off, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/genomecov.html
  column: plus_share_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: median plus-strand share, of 100

- component: card
  title: Strongest window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest signal of any 250 kb window, in parts per million of its library, and the strip gives the median and the upper quartile of a window. It answers how far the hottest window sits above a typical one.
    How to read: a maximum many times above the upper quartile marks a hotspot, such as a ribosomal array. Use the table to find which window and library hold it.
  column: signal_rpm
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median and upper quartile of a window

- component: interactive
  title: Chromosome
  description: Filters every tile of the dashboard that reads these windows to the chromosomes picked here.
    It answers how a library behaves on one chromosome at a time.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: chromosome

- component: table
  title: Strand signal per window
  description: |-
    Each row is a 250 kb window of one library, with the plus and minus strand signal in parts per million, their sum, its log2 and the plus-strand share. It answers the exact value behind every other tile.
    How to read: sort by signal to find the strongest windows, or filter by chromosome and library to compare the same region across libraries.

- component: card
  title: Plus-strand share per library
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of a library's signal on the plus strand, shown against 100 percent, with the lowest and highest library beside it. It answers whether libraries read both strands evenly.
    How to read: a library far from the others, or far from 50, has one strand dominating, which can be a protocol or strandedness problem. Open the bar tile below to see which library it is.
    Note: bedtools genomecov reports one strand at a time with the -strand option and publishes no balance cut-off, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/genomecov.html
  column: plus_share_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: median plus-strand share, of 100

- component: card
  title: Signal held by hotspot windows
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the chromosome signal held by the top 1 percent of 250 kb windows of a library, and the box shows the spread across libraries. It answers how concentrated the signal is.
    How to read: a high share means a few windows, such as ribosomal arrays or very active loci, take most of the reads and the rest of the genome is read from what is left. A library well above the others is the one to check first.
    Note: the top 1 percent is a fixed definition of this recipe, not a cut-off published by bedtools.
  column: hotspot_share_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Read bases per library
  description: |-
    The hero number is the read bases summed over every library and both strands, and the bar splits them by library, with the median and maximum library beside it. It answers how evenly depth is shared between libraries.
    How to read: a library with a thin share has far less depth than the others, so its signal is noisier. Compare libraries in parts per million, as the genome tiles do, and not in raw bases.
  column: total_read_bases
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: sample
  caption: read bases, by library

- component: figure
  title: Plus-strand share per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library, with the percent of its signal on the plus strand. It answers which library reads one strand more than the others.
    How to read: bars near one another mean a consistent protocol. A bar far from the rest has lost or gained a strand and deserves a check of the library preparation.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median plus-strand share of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bedtools. bedtools genomecov reports one strand at a time and publishes no balance cut-off.
    Source: https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/content/tools/genomecov.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: plus_share_pct
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Library
      plus_share_pct: Plus-strand share (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: plus_share_pct

- component: figure
  title: Hotspot share against signal outside the chromosomes
  description: |-
    Each point is a library, with the share of its chromosome signal held by the hottest windows on the horizontal axis and the share of reads outside the main chromosomes on the vertical axis. It answers which libraries are dominated by a few loci or by unplaced contigs.
    How to read: points toward the upper right combine a concentrated signal with many reads off the chromosomes, a pattern of a poorly depleted library. Points near the origin spread their reads over the chromosomes.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median share of signal outside the chromosomes of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bedtools. Both shares are defined by the recipe, and bedtools genomecov publishes no cut-off for either.
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: hotspot_share_pct
    y: off_main_pct
    color: sample
    hover_name: sample
    labels:
      hotspot_share_pct: Signal in top 1% windows (%)
      off_main_pct: Signal outside chromosomes (%)
      sample: Library
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: off_main_pct
    label: Median signal outside chromosomes

- component: table
  title: Strand coverage per library
  description: |-
    Each row is a library, with its read bases per strand, the covered megabases, the deepest base and the plus-strand, mitochondrial, off-chromosome and hotspot shares. It answers the exact numbers behind every other tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by hotspot share or by mitochondrial share to find the libraries that need a closer look.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample
